primitives.name: State-Space Hurdle Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model Hurdle state-space model: Pr(y_t=0) = π_t (π_t=1 when market closed); log(y_t)|y_t>0 ~ N(μ_t, σ); μ_t = ν_t + s_t with linear predictor ν_t = x_t^{(1)'}β; latent market-activity s_t an ARX(1): s_t = φs_{t-1} + x_t^{(2)'}ω + σ_s ε_t, |φ|<1.
primitives.latex:
\begin{aligned}
\text{Pr}(y_t = 0) &= \pi_t \\
\log(y_t) \mid y_t > 0 &\sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_t, \sigma) \\
\mu_t &= \nu_t + s_t \\
\nu_t &= x_t^{(1)'}\beta \\
s_t &= \varphi s_{t-1} + x_t^{(2)'}\omega + \sigma_s \varepsilon_t
\end{aligned}

reasoning_traces.think:
The core idea of the paper is to model live betting volume using a state-space hurdle model, which separates the probability of zero stakes from the distribution of positive stakes. This allows for capturing both the occurrence of betting and its magnitude. The model uses two components: a logistic regression for the hurdle (zero-stake probability) and a normal distribution for the positive stakes. The key innovation lies in modeling the latent market activity as an ARX(1) process, incorporating past activity and exogenous variables. The authors derive a discretized hidden Markov model approximation to enable maximum likelihood estimation. However, they do not implement actual fraud detection, leaving it as future work. The failure mode arises from the lack of validation metrics or flagged matches, rendering the model speculative without empirical testing. The model’s strength lies in its ability to capture temporal dependencies in betting behavior, which could be repurposed for GSE's edge-finding applications by treating residuals as predictive signals rather than fraud indicators.
